title: Technical Deep Dive - Multi-region routing & failover
summary: SE-led deep dive covering multi-region routing policies, regional capacity planning, DR playbooks, and runtime considerations (KV cache, batching, quantization) for an on-prem/VPC-sensitive deployment. Customer is concerned about cross-region failover, cache warm-up, and compliance implications for DR traffic.
topics: Policy routing (latency vs cost vs capacity)
KV cache behavior across regions and cache warming
Quantization and model variants during failover
VPC / on-prem routing constraints and egress/data residency
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:15 UTC
Duration: ~62 min
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Tom, Lily, Markus, Priya (Aegis)

Auto-summary: SE walkthrough of routing architecture diagrams, policy examples, and DR playbooks; discussed implications for KV cache and batching when failing over to another region and how Redwood handles model variants and quantized fallbacks. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alicia: hi everyone thanks for joining, uh quick note we're recording, uh i've got ravi and jenna on to dive into the design.
[00:28] Tom: thanks, yeah we've been looking to validate our DR strategy, specifically how requests get routed if the primary eu-west region goes down, and what happens to in-flight sessions.
[00:46] Ravi: yeah great question. so at a high level we do policy based routing - you can define priorities: latency-first, cost-first, capacity-aware. default is latency-first with soft-fail to nearest compatible model variant.
[01:15] Lily: when you say compatible variant, do you mean a quantized model or smaller architecture? we need to understand quality degradation during failover.
[01:33] Jenna: right so we support variant maps in the deployment config. e.g. gpt-4x -> gpt-4x-q4 or gpt-4-small as a last resort. we expose a compatibility matrix and expected perf/quality deltas.
[02:02] Markus: what about KV cache? if a session is in eu-west and we fail to us-east, is the cache lost and do we have to re-warm? that has big latency implications.
[02:21] Ravi: correct, kv cache is local to the serving instance. when you failover across region we surface two options: synchronous cross-region replicate (for warm cache but higher cost / latency during normal ops) or cold failover where cache is rebuilt. for financial latency-sensitive flows we usually recommend hybrid: replicate critical prefixes for authenticated sessions, and allow best-effort rewarm for others.
[03:04] Tom: okay can you quantify rewarm cost? like how many tokens of extra latency are we talking?
[03:13] Jenna: depends on sequence length and prompt shape, but in our runs we saw a median rewarm penalty of 200-800ms for typical short prompts when KV is cold, and up to multiple seconds for long context where KV saved a lot. we shared a benchmark spreadsheet in the deck (link: internal - bench/apex-region-cache).
[03:47] Priya: quick security question - if we replicate KV cross-region, does any user data land in another jurisdiction? we need to ensure data residency controls.
[03:58] Ravi: replication respects routing and tenancy. in Redwood Private you can configure which regions are permitted for replication and we integrate with your KMS/HSM so keys don't leave allowed zones. we also provide audit logs for replication events.
[04:28] Lily: what about batching when you failover? i.e., if a region suddenly takes additional traffic, batching behavior could increase latency tail. how does the runtime preserve SLOs?
[04:45] Jenna: runtime has workload-aware batching that tunes target batch sizes by latency SLO. when surge happens we do two things: dynamic max batch size reduction for latency-critical routes and prioritized queues for canary or high-tier traffic. that reduces throughput but keeps p99 in check.
[05:18] Markus: so there's a throughput vs latency trade-off, right? we need predictable degradation.
[05:25] Ravi: exactly. we recommend pre-configured degrade policies: step-down quantization (auto-apply q4 when latency spikes), and routing fallback to regions with reserved dedicated capacity for high-tier customers.
[05:55] Tom: dedicated capacity - how is that integrated with multi-region failover? can we reserve dedicated pools in two regions and failover without capacity exhaust?
[06:12] Jenna: yes, you can reserve Dedicated pools in multiple regions and assign them as failover targets. autoscaling policies can be set to pre-warm a buffer on the standby region during business hours; we also support scheduled dr-drills where we simulate failover.
[06:38] Lily: concerning scheduled drills - when you flip traffic, do you get consistent model versions across regions? we've seen drift cause quality diffs.
[06:50] Ravi: deployments include model pins and rollout policies. you pin specific model versions to avoid drift and we can do canary route tests pre-failover. also model archives and checksums are verified during deployment.
[07:19] Tom: runbook question: what's the typical DR playbook for a region outage? step-by-step.
[07:28] Jenna: high level: 1) detect and notify; 2) automatically re-route per policy (immediate soft-fail to nearest compatible region); 3) if latency exceeds threshold, escalate to reserve dedicated pool failover; 4) run cache-rewarm jobs for critical users; 5) post-mortem and audit log generation. we have a template playbook we can share.
[08:01] Priya: how about compliance - will failing over mean logs or customer data traverse new providers? our legal team needs a clear statement.
[08:12] Alicia: we'll attach the security docs and a redwood-private runbook excerpt. also our SOC2 and encryption details.
[08:22] Lily: can you walk through a concrete scenario: eu-west primary fails at 9:00, 5k rps moves to us-east which has 2x capacity in steady state but only 1x available for us because of other traffic. show us latency curve and recommended policy.
[08:44] Ravi: sure, let me share my screen - (screen share) - here's a simulation. policy A: latency-first with soft-fail to us-east. policy B: capacity-aware which shards by customer tier. with A you see p50 jump ~20%, p95 jumps 40-80% depending on KV rewarm. with B you see a slower degradation because we shed low-tier traffic to cheaper region and preserve high-tier SLOs.
[09:32] Tom: okay interesting. what artifacts do you provide to verify prior to go-live? we want a bench we can run in our environment.
[09:40] Jenna: we provide a benchmarking harness and a checklist: (1) synthetic traffic generator template; (2) regional capacity spreadsheet; (3) sample failover test scripts; (4) step-by-step playbook. we'll drop links after the call.
[10:05] Lily: on the quantization side, if we fallback to q4 models during failover, do you apply any dynamic prompt rewriting to preserve quality?
[10:18] Ravi: we support prompt shaping and lightweight reranking. we suggest a small prompt prefix to reduce hallucination risk in lower-capacity models. for critical flows we recommend A/B tests prior to enabling auto-quantize.
[10:40] Markus: any gotchas with VPC/private deployments? like cross-VPC peering when failing to another region?
[10:50] Jenna: two common patterns: 1) egress via your transit gateway to the failover region (you manage network peering) - that keeps data path within your network; 2) we can proxy via Redwood Private control plane if you permit cross-region egress under a bounded policy. both require network changes and firewall rules.
[11:18] Tom: latency - if traffic is backhauled across region inside our colo, that could add 100s ms. do you have guidance for network topologies?
[11:28] Ravi: we recommend colocating dedicated pools or using cross-region private links with minimal hops. we also have guidance doc: network topology for multi-region inference.
[11:44] Priya: audit trail for failover decisioning - where is that stored?
[11:51] Alicia: audit logs are stored in your log destination or our audit bucket depending on deployment; in Redwood Private we push to your SIEM via syslog/s3. every routing decision gets a trace id for correlation.
[12:08] Lily: can we simulate cache warming prior to traffic cutover? like prefetching top-k prompts for premium users?
[12:17] Jenna: yes, we support pre-warm jobs that inject prefix contexts into the KV cache across target region instances. recommended approach: run warmers for top 10% of sessions and monitor success rates.
[12:34] Markus: what about session affinity? can we preserve holder session ids between regions?
[12:40] Ravi: session affinity is best-effort and depends on your load balancer. our client SDK supports sticky routing with fallbacks; on cross-region failover you get a new session id but we can carry session metadata if you push to a shared metadata store.
[13:05] Tom: operationally, we want to avoid surprise cost spikes in a failover. what controls exist?
[13:13] Jenna: you can set budget caps per region and automated billing alerts. plus route policies can include cost ceilings that steer traffic away when near budget.
[13:26] Lily: are there any built in throttles during failover to protect the standby region?
[13:32] Ravi: yes throttles and rate-limits can be attached to routes. additionally, we support token-based priority queues for premium customers.
[13:52] Priya: security again: when we do cross-region replication for KV, is the KV encrypted at rest and in transit? who has the keys?
[14:02] Alicia: encrypted in transit with TLS, at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). you control the keys in Private deployment. in Hosted we can also support customer KMS via key wrapping options.
[14:20] Markus: you mentioned trace ids - can we link those to our tracing system?
[14:25] Jenna: yes we add correlation headers and you can ingest traces into your tracing backend.
[14:39] Tom: timeframe - if we wanted this dual-region Dedicated pool with a DR playbook, how long to provision?
[14:47] Ravi: provisioning Dedicated pools typically 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and hardware requirements; for Private on-prem it depends on network setup and procurement, typically 6-12 weeks.
[15:05] Lily: do you support region affinity by customer or route? we want some customers to stay in-eu only.
[15:12] Alicia: yes, routing policies can be per-customer, per-route, or global. you can tag customers and apply region allowlists.
[15:25] Tom: show of hands - any open questions on model quality during failover?
[15:31] Lily: i'd like to run an eval on our top 200 prompts with q4 vs full float to see drift.
[15:37] Jenna: we'll run slice-level evals and add regression alerts to Redwood Optimize if you want.
[15:45] Markus: cost model for replication? what's the incremental cost to keep KV synched?
[15:52] Ravi: depends on replication frequency and payload size; rough rule: cross-region KV replication adds 10-25% to token serving costs for heavy replication but saves rewarm latency. we'll provide a cost model sheet.
[16:10] Tom: what about legal signoff for cross-border failover? we will need explicit contract language.
[16:18] Alicia: we'll loop legal and provide contract language examples used with other financial customers.
[16:27] Lily: can you explain the failure detection criteria so we know what counts as region outage vs transient degradation?
[16:34] Jenna: detection uses multi-signal heuristics: health probes, RTT thresholds, error rates, infra-level alarms. thresholds are configurable per route. we also emit an incident severity that maps to failover behaviour.
[16:52] Markus: is there manual override? e.g., hold failover until SRE approves?
[16:56] Ravi: yes you can set manual-only failover for critical paths or set an approval workflow via the Console.
[17:10] Tom: operational play - during failover do you run a rollout verification to check quality on a small traffic slice first?
[17:18] Jenna: yes we recommend canary slices. the platform supports gradual ramp and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected (via configured evals).
[17:35] Lily: a couple specific questions on quantization: 1) do you do per-layer quant tuning? 2) can we lock certain layers to float?
[17:44] Ravi: we do per-component quant profiles and you can create custom quant bundles; locking layers is supported in the model config.
[18:02] Tom: are these controls in the Console or infra-as-code?
[18:06] Jenna: both - Console for quick config and YAML spec for infra-as-code. all changes are auditable.
[18:18] Priya: what about secrets management during failover (API keys, model keys)?
[18:24] Alicia: keys remain in your KMS; we don't re-encrypt with new keys during failover unless you rotate them. access policies follow your IAM permissions.
[18:36] Lily: curious about cold-start behaviors - if a whole model isn't present in standby region, do you pull model artifacts on demand? what's the time?
[18:45] Ravi: model pull times depend on model size and network. for large models (>50GB) cold pull could be minutes; that's why we recommend artifact pre-stage for critical models. for quantized variants size shrinks and pull times are shorter.
[19:10] Tom: what's the recommended approach for long-context KV-heavy workflows?
[19:16] Jenna: replicate critical prefixes and pre-warm; also consider hybrid routing where user sessions route to region-of-record unless explicit failover.
[19:30] Markus: any tooling for visualizing routing decisions and capacity per region?
[19:35] Alicia: Console shows per-route dashboards, capacity heatmaps, and a simulated failover view you can run.
[19:47] Lily: ok let's capture next steps so we can take this to our infra and legal teams.
[19:54] Alicia: yep - i'll recap.
[20:00] --- Recap and next steps ---
[20:03] Alicia: 1) we'll share the DR playbook template and routing policy examples. 2) ravi/jenna will share benchmarking harness and regional capacity spreadsheet. 3) we will schedule a follow-up failover drill in a sandbox run by the 2nd week of april. 4) provide contract language for cross-border failover. 5) run a q4 vs float eval on your top 200 prompts.
[20:28] Tom: sounds good, timeline for artifacts?
[20:31] Jenna: we'll send docs by 2026-03-09.
[20:35] Lily: i'll coordinate with legal and security for required signoffs.
[20:40] Alicia: thanks all. any final quick q's?
[20:45] Markus: none here.
[20:48] Priya: nothing.
[20:50] Alicia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the sandbox drill.
[20:55] (call ends)
